title: The Artifact governs a class of off-chain parameters that no contract enforces
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2.1.1.2 defines a distinct parameter class: "off-chain operational parameters for the Spark Liquidity Layer on each blockchain. These operational parameters are protocol settings managed outside of smart contracts (off-chain), used by operators and off-chain systems to guide the functioning of the Spark Liquidity Layer."

The distinction matters because the two parameter classes have entirely different enforcement. The ALM rate limits are contracts: a Relayer physically cannot exceed them. A minimum operation size or a target USDC balance is a number an operator is expected to respect, with nothing on-chain stopping a violation.

Writing them into the Artifact anyway is the right call. It makes the operating policy inspectable and gives deviations a reference to be judged against — a breach becomes visible and attributable rather than a matter of opinion about what operators should have done.

But it also means the Artifact's parameters are not uniformly binding, and nothing in the naming tells a casual reader which kind they are looking at beyond the section they sit under. When assessing what the Liquidity Layer *can* do versus what it is *supposed* to do, the on-chain limits give the hard bound and the off-chain parameters give the intended behaviour inside it.
description: Off-Chain Operational Parameters are 'protocol settings managed outside of smart contracts' used by operators and off-chain systems — governed text whose only enforcement is operator compliance.
